items.title: Section: When Is an Object Truly "Present"? Distance for the Eye, Contact for the Tongue, and an Owl's Night Vision

items.zh: 謂色於眼，非合、非闇、非極細遠、亦非有障，名為現前；要唯有見、有明、無障、在可行處，乃名現前。又於一眼雖闇障色，亦名現前。聲於耳根，亦必非合、非極細遠，得名現前；有障無障、若明若闇，在可行處，皆名現前。香、味、觸三，於鼻、舌、身，唯合能取，在可行處，乃名現前所行境界。若諸天眼，唯照有見，有障無障、若明若闇、若近若遠，皆名現前。然在可行處，非不可行處。若聖慧眼，一切種色皆是所行。
items.en: For colour with respect to the eye — neither in contact, nor in darkness, nor extremely minute or distant, nor obstructed — this is called present; only being visible, illuminated, unobstructed, and within range is called present. Yet for a certain single kind of eye, colour remains present even when obscured by darkness. For sound with respect to the ear — likewise neither in contact nor extremely faint or distant — this is called present; whether obstructed or not, whether light or dark, within range, all of this is called present. Smell, taste, and touch, with respect to nose, tongue, and body, are grasped only through contact; within range, this is called the present object of activity. The divine eye illuminates only what is visible, yet whether obstructed or not, light or dark, near or far, all of this is called present — provided it lies within range, not beyond it. The wise eye of the noble ones takes every kind of matter whatsoever as its domain.

items.zh: 問：如本地分說六種所行性，此何差別耶？答：初所行性，謂有情世間所攝色，及器世間所攝色。第

items.title: Section: What Damages a Sense Faculty — And a Modern Meditator Fleeing a Retreat on the Fourth Day

items.zh: 二所行性，謂由三自性自性差別故，相差別故，作
items.en:
Through two conditions: partial impairment and total destruction. Their absence should be known as undamaged. Furthermore, briefly, the faculties vary through four conditions. First, arising from external conditions... or from the benefit or harm of other beings. Second, arising from internal conditions. Third, arising from karmic conditions, meaning past karma's own dominant power brings about attractiveness or unattractiveness. Fourth, arising from the faculty's own inherent variation, meaning the faculties' own particular distinctions.
Through four conditions. First, caused by a hindrance, meaning one of the five hindrances obscuring the mind. Second, caused by disturbance, meaning malevolent spirits disturbing the mind. Third, caused by what is not yet attained, meaning the mind, not having yet attained the excellent qualities of absorption or the formless attainments, forcibly generates intention towards them regardless. Fourth, caused by what is not yet understood, meaning the mind, not yet proficient in extensive learning or skilled work, forcibly applies effort regardless.

items.title: Section: Mind Alone Creates the Scene — Six Ways an Object Becomes "Present," and the Attention That Completes It

items.zh: 色相差別者，謂青、黃、赤、白等，乃至廣說。作用差別者，謂有表、無表、律儀、不律儀、非律儀非不律儀所攝作用。分位差別者，謂可意、不可意色，及順捨處色。聲相差別者，謂執受大種為因、非執受大種為因、執受非執受大種為因。作用差別者，謂語表業。分位差別者，如前應知。香相差別者，謂根、莖、皮、實、華、葉、果香。作用差別者，謂香、味、觸皆無作用。分位差別，如前應知。味相差別者，謂甘苦等。如前已說。觸相差別，亦如前說多種應知。第三所行性，謂東、南、西、北等方維差別應知。第四所行性，謂過去、未來、現在差別應知。第五所行性，謂取實不實差別應知。第六所行性，謂取一分事、或遍滿事差別應知。如是等類，是名諸色境界現前差別應知。云何名為能生作意。謂由所依不壞故、境界現前故，所起能引發心所。如是等類，應當思惟色蘊所行相。
items.en:
Colour's distinctions of character are blue, yellow, red, white, and so on as extensively explained... sound's distinctions of character are sound caused by a sentient being's own matter, sound caused by non-sentient matter, and sound caused by both combined... smell, taste, and touch all lack any function... the third kind of object-of-activity is the distinction of the eight directions. The fourth is the distinction of past, future, and present. The fifth is the distinction of grasping a real or unreal object. The sixth is the distinction of grasping a portion or the whole.
What is called the attention that generates perception? It is the mental factor which arises and rouses consciousness, given an undamaged basis and a present object. Things of this kind are how form aggregate's own domain of activity should be contemplated.

items.title: Section: Like Sand Settled in Water — How Two Realms' Matter Share One Body, and Why Every Act Leaves Its Mark

items.zh: 復次，在欲界者，依欲界身發起色界大種現前，彼諸大種云何與下界色共住？為異處耶、非異處耶？當言如水處沙，非住異處。如是等類，應當思惟色蘊互相雜住。
items.en: Furthermore, for one in the desire realm, when form-realm elements arise depending on a desire-realm body, how do those elements coexist with matter of the lower realm — do they dwell in a different location, or not a different location? It should be said they are like sand settled within water, not dwelling in a different location. Things of this kind are how form aggregate's mutual intermixing should be contemplated.

blocks.text: A short day: when does an object count as "present" to a sense? The answer ends with attention: without it, nothing is fully taken in.

Master Cháng Bǎi: to the eye a colour must be at some distance, not merged with it; smell, taste, and touch must be in contact. Some eyes, like an owl's, see clearly even in darkness. Sound, not in contact and not too faint, is present whether obstructed or not, within range.

External, internal, and karmic conditions, and the faculty's own variation. Forcing the mind towards absorption not yet attained, or forcing effort in skills not yet mastered, damages the mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: so attention must not be forced. (Untranslated, 0600c29: how this differs from the six kinds of object-range in the Basic Section.)

Sound arises from elements held by the store-consciousness (a bird's song), from elements not held, or from both. Attention is "the mental factor arising from an undamaged basis and a present object, which rouses consciousness". Master Cháng Bǎi: attention is needed for an object to be fully taken in.
The matter of two realms shares one body "like sand settled in water". Master Cháng Bǎi: form-realm matter is exceedingly subtle and does not obstruct desire-realm matter.

Consciousness, the aggregates, and matter, analysed closely. The thread: things are processes, matter is subtler than it looks, and attention decides what becomes present. For practice, the warning about forcing the mind may be the most useful line of all.

quiz.q: When is colour said to be present to the eye?
options: not in contact, dark, extremely minute or distant, or obstructed; visible, lit, unobstructed, and within range
it must be in contact with the eye, lit and unobstructed, clearest of all when pressed right against it
whether light or dark, obstructed or not, it is present
it is present whenever mental consciousness thinks of it
quiz.why: The treatise sets out the conditions for colour. Master Cháng Bǎi: to the eye faculty a colour must have some distance and not be merged with it; whereas smell, taste, and touch must be in close contact with nose, tongue, and body to function. Sound differs again: for the ear, light or dark makes no difference.

quiz.q: The English has "even amid darkness and obstruction" for 雖闇障色. According to the Sub-commentary, what is meant, and what is wrong?
options: a kind means the divine eye, unhindered by dark and walls, so the English is right, the divine eye seeing through walls as here
a kind means the buddha eye, and the English should say so
certain physical eyes, as of owls, are not hindered by the obstacle of dark; 闇障 is one thing, and the English makes two, as if seeing through walls
a kind means a blind person's eye, and the English should say so
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary explains this as a kind of physical eye, like an owl's, for which colour counts as present despite the obstacle of darkness. Master Cháng Bǎi: such eyes see clearly even with the obstruction of dark. The English "darkness and obstruction" reads as two, which would have an owl seeing through walls; "obstructed or not" is said only of the divine eye.

quiz.q: What are the conditions of presence for sound to the ear, and for the divine eye?
options: sound must touch the ear and is unheard in the dark; the divine eye has no limit of range, seeing every world in all directions
sound needs light and no obstruction; the divine eye sees only what is near
sound and the divine eye both require contact with the faculty
sound, not in contact or too faint, is present obstructed or not, light or dark; the divine eye likewise, near or far, but within range
quiz.why: The treatise says sound, not in contact nor extremely faint, is present whether obstructed or not, light or dark, within range. The divine eye too sees whether obstructed or not, near or far, but only within range. Master Cháng Bǎi: light or dark makes no difference to hearing; and beyond the range of the divine eye one cannot see. Even the divine eye has limits.

quiz.q: Through which four conditions do the faculties vary?
options: caused by a hindrance, disturbance, what is not attained, and what is not understood, all being why the mental faculty loses mastery
arising from external conditions, internal conditions, karmic conditions, and the faculty's own inherent variation
imbalance of earth, water, fire, and wind
the four sufferings of birth, ageing, sickness, and death
quiz.why: The treatise names external, internal, and karmic conditions and the faculty's own variation. Master Cháng Bǎi: besides present conditions, the karma of past lives also changes the five faculties; improper attention breeding afflictions damages the six faculties, while the absorption and wisdom born of proper attention benefit them. The second option is the list for the mental faculty.

quiz.q: On damage to the mental faculty from what is not attained or understood, what does Master Cháng Bǎi caution?
options: the more one forces practice the better, for only force breaks through; not attaining simply means too little effort
one who has not attained should not practise until the fruit is reached
attention must not be forced; forcing what one cannot do also harms the mental faculty
one who has not understood should not study until awakened
quiz.why: The treatise says the mind forcibly generates intention towards absorption it has not attained, or forcibly applies effort in learning or skills it has not mastered. Master Cháng Bǎi: so attention must not be forced; forcing what one cannot do also harms the mental faculty. The caution matters for meditators pushing beyond their capacity.

quiz.q: What three distinctions of sound does the treatise give?
options: wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral sound
sound caused by appropriated elements, by non-appropriated elements, and by both together
past, future, and present sound, divided by time, unrelated to the elements producing them
high, middle, and low sound
quiz.why: The treatise divides sound by its cause: appropriated elements, non-appropriated elements, and both. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is sound from elements appropriated by the store-consciousness, such as birdsong or the croak of a frog. The English "a sentient being's own matter" conveys the sense but loses both 執受 and 大種.

quiz.q: What is the attention that generates, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say of its importance?
options: an outer force arising from the object itself, unrelated to the basis; the treatise holds objects are taken fully without attention
another name for the store-consciousness, generating all seeds
a general name for wholesome factors, found only in practice
the factor arising from an undamaged basis and a present object that rouses mind; attention is needed to fully take an object
quiz.why: The treatise defines it as the mental factor arising from an undamaged basis and a present object, which rouses consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: attention is required for an object to be fully taken. Note the English heading "generates perception" adds a word, since what attention rouses here is consciousness, as the English sentence itself says.

quiz.q: When form-realm elements arise in a desire-realm body, how do they coexist with lower-realm matter?
options: they dwell in different places, form-realm elements above and outside the body, and the two never touch
like sand and water, not in a different location; form-realm matter is very subtle, not obstructing, and intermixes
desire-realm matter must first cease wholly before they arise
form-realm elements press upon lower matter, making the body heavy
quiz.why: The treatise says they are like sand settled in water, not in a different location. Master Cháng Bǎi: form-realm matter is exceedingly subtle and does not obstruct desire-realm matter; the elements of the form-realm divine eye dwell where the elements of the physical eye dwell, intermixed. This closes the ten aspects of the form aggregate; the other four aggregates follow in the next fascicle.
